# Four ways to approximate
Every numerical method builds its answer in one of four ways. Each result below says which, and how far it was pushed.

## 1. Series and expansions
An infinite sum, cut off after a few terms. The Taylor polynomial is exact at the centre and drifts away from it; the Chebyshev polynomial spreads the error evenly over an interval.

cells.exprs: exp(x) - T(x), exp(x) - Ch(x), exp(x) - P(x)

cells.source: series_solve(D(y, x) == x + y, y, x, 0, 1)

## 2. Iterative methods
Start from a guess and refine it until the change is below a tolerance. Newton doubles the correct digits at every step; fixed-point iteration gains them slowly.

## 3. Discretized methods
The continuous problem is replaced by a grid. Finite differences approximate derivatives with neighbouring points; finite elements approximate the solution with simple pieces. Compare the boundary value problem $y'' = -y$, $y(0) = 0$, $y(\pi/2) = 1$ with its exact solution $\sin x$.
y_fd = fdm_solve(D(y, x, 2) == -y, y, x, 0, 0, pi/2, 1, 10)

## 4. Time-stepping methods
An initial value problem advanced one step at a time. With the same step, Euler's method drifts visibly while RK4 sits on the exact curve $e^{-2x}$.
